subject.title: Anthropic setup-token onboarding path has multiple failure modes (docs gap, credential propagation, multi-agent sync)

question: Should Anthropic setup-token/manual-token auth be made available to sibling agents by runtime inheritance, by write-time copying of portable static tokens, or by a separate explicit sync/doctor flow?
rationale: The current source shows unresolved write-side gaps, but prior sibling-copy PRs raised credential propagation and OAuth fanout concerns that automation should not decide as a security boundary.

options.title: Prefer inheritance plus validation
options.body: Keep main-store read-through as the default, improve setup-token prompts, and add readback/diagnostic validation so users get a clear repair path without duplicating credentials.

options.title: Allow static-token sibling copies
options.body: Permit write-time fanout only for explicitly portable static token credentials, with tests proving OAuth refresh material remains opt-in or non-portable.

options.title: Use an explicit sync or doctor repair
options.body: Leave setup-token writes scoped to one agent and add a visible operator command or doctor fix for bulk credential propagation and shadowing recovery.

recommendation.title: Prefer inheritance plus validation
recommendation.body: Keep main-store read-through as the default, improve setup-token prompts, and add readback/diagnostic validation so users get a clear repair path without duplicating credentials.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has recent commits on the central auth write paths and provided the clearest maintainer signal on auth-file security in the prior linked PR.
